title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: archive files classified as one object on Windows
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's archive-classification notice, including the affected organisations, unchanged policy evaluation and rollout windows. The licensing, audit-search path and PowerShell command are supported by the cited Microsoft documentation.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The affected organisations use Endpoint DLP on Windows endpoints with archive file classification enabled.
claims.quote: Organizations using Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP on Windows endpoints with archive file classification enabled

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice gives .zip and .rar as examples of archive files affected by the change.
claims.quote: Archive files such as .zip and .rar files will be classified directly.

claims.claim: Archive files will be classified directly.
claims.quote: Archive files such as .zip and .rar files will be classified directly.

claims.claim: An archive will be classified as one object in a single atomic operation.
claims.quote: Archive files will be classified as a single atomic object and reported as the outer archive file rather than generating separate events for files within the archive.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Individual files inside an archive will no longer generate separate classification events.
claims.quote: Individual files contained within an archive will no longer generate separate classification events.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: Reporting will identify the outer archive instead of producing separate events for its individual files.
claims.quote: Only the outer archive file will be reported in Endpoint DLP events.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Context-based policy evaluation continues to apply to content within archives.
claims.quote: Context-based and sensitivity label-based policy evaluation will continue to apply to content within archive files.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Sensitivity label-based policy evaluation continues to apply to content within archives.
claims.quote: Context-based and sensitivity label-based policy evaluation will continue to apply to content within archive files.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing DLP policy behaviour for evaluating archive content is unchanged.
claims.quote: Existing DLP policy behavior for evaluating content within archive files is unchanged.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor MC1474107 describes a meter or consumption charge for the change.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "archive" "classification" "licensing" "price". Read the complete roadmap record and MC1474107; neither names a meter or consumption charge. Opened the Purview service description, which lists Endpoint DLP as Included.

claims.claim: Learn lists .zip, .rar, .7z and .tar among the archive types monitored by Endpoint DLP.
claims.quote: | Archive | Zip, RAR, 7z, TAR | `.zip, .rar, .7z, .tar, .gz, .arj, .bz2, .cab, .chm, .lzh, .lzma, .mhtml, .xar, .xz` |

claims.claim: At the time of writing, the cited Endpoint DLP Learn page does not describe the new single-object archive-reporting behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "archive" "atomic" "outer". Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about and searched its full fetched text for archive, atomic, classification, .zip and .rar; archive formats are listed but the new reporting behaviour is not described.

claims.claim: The notice does not say that the change reads new data.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP archive file classification behavior change Windows identity roles new automated actions data accessed MC1474107. Read MC1474107, including Compliance considerations; it describes atomic classification and outer-archive reporting, not newly read data.

claims.claim: No identity or role change is described for this update.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP archive file classification behavior change Windows identity roles new automated actions data accessed MC1474107. Read the complete supplied notice and roadmap record and opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about; no identity or role change for this update is described.

claims.claim: No new automated action is described beyond the classification and reporting change.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP archive file classification behavior change Windows identity roles new automated actions data accessed MC1474107. Read the supplied notice and roadmap record; existing policy behaviour is unchanged and no additional automated action is described.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing internal documentation about archive file classification.
claims.quote: Review internal documentation that describes archive file classification behavior.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating operational and monitoring procedures that reference individual events for files inside archives.
claims.quote: Update operational and monitoring procedures if they reference individual event generation for files contained within archives.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends informing compliance and security teams about outer-archive reporting.
claims.quote: Inform compliance and security teams that Endpoint DLP reporting will show events for the outer archive file instead of individual files within the archive.

claims.claim: Audit search is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Audit > Search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <ExDateTime> -EndDate <ExDateTime> searches unified audit records over a date range.
claims.quote:
Use the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet to search the unified audit log. ... Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>

claims.claim: The listed audit search is a read-only review operation, not a classification switch.
claims.quote: You can search for all events in a specified date range, or you can filter the results based on specific criteria, such as the user who performed the action, the action, or the target object.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching the audit log requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls

claims.claim: Activity explorer takes its activity data from Microsoft 365 unified audit logs.
claims.quote: The activity information comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit logs. It's transformed and then made available in the activity explorer UI.

claims.claim: Activity explorer is another place analysts can read Endpoint DLP events.
claims.quote: When you enable Endpoint data loss prevention (DLP), Activity Explorer also includes device-level activities from onboarded Windows 10, Windows 11, and the three most recent major macOS versions.

claims.claim: Audit search is an organisation-wide, tenant-scoped review control.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.
